:::{#thm-hyperplane-graph}
#### The graph of an affine function is a hyperplane

Let $\vec{w} \in \reals^p$, $b \in \reals$.
The [graph](functions.qmd#def-graph) of the [function](functions.qmd#def-function) $\vx \mapsto \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx} + b$ is the [set](sets.qmd#def-set)

$$
\cb{\sbmat{\vx \\ y} \in \reals^{p+1} : y = \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx} + b}.
$$

This set is a [hyperplane](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-hyperplane) in $\reals^{p+1}$,
with [normal vector](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-normal-vector) $\sbmat{\vec{w} \\ -1}$.

:::

:::{.proof}
For $\sbmat{\vx \\ y} \in \reals^{p+1}$,

$$
\ba
y = \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx} + b
&\iff \dprod{\vec{w}}{\vx} - y + b = 0
&& \text{(subtract } y \text{ from both sides)}
\\
&\iff \dprod{\sbmat{\vec{w} \\ -1}}{\sbmat{\vx \\ y}} + b = 0.
&& \text{(dot product of stacked vectors)}
\ea
$$

So the [set](sets.qmd#def-set) is the solution set of the equation in @def-hyperplane, with [normal vector](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-normal-vector) $\sbmat{\vec{w} \\ -1}$.
That vector is nonzero, because its last entry is $-1$.
:::
